filename: Immediate and Long‐Lasting Impacts of the Mt.pdf
title: Immediate and Long-Lasting Impacts of the Mt. Pinatubo Eruption on Ocean Oxygen and Carbon Inventories
code_availability: The CESM source code is freely available at http://www2.cesm.ucar.edu.
testbed_rationale: The datasets consist of nominal 1-degree global coupled Earth system model ensemble simulations focused on biogeochemical and physical climate response to volcanic forcing, without high-resolution process-resolving benchmark simulations for ML parameterization.
pain_points: Large internal climate variability masks forced signals in surface air-sea fluxes at regional and grid scales.
Aerosol forcing files in CESM1 underestimate aerosol loading in the Southern Hemisphere following the Pinatubo eruption.
Coarse nominal 1-degree resolution leads to known biases in tropical oxygen minimum zones, equatorial ventilation, and diapycnal mixing over rough topography.
extraction_notes: The paper does not develop or evaluate machine learning methods; it applies Earth system model large ensemble numerical experiments to isolate volcanic climate and ocean biogeochemical impacts.
